## What This Is

Two coupled changes that travel as one. First, a new **Primer** surface: the canonical forward handoff your AI reads first at every session start, pre-loaded so a fresh download opens to orientation rather than a blank file. Second, the Session Closeout collapses to a single lean close built around it. The two are a unit. The close can be three fast actions precisely because the Primer holds the rolling horizon, so nothing has to bloat Sovereign Command, which stays the minimal glance it was always meant to be. This supersedes the closeout half of v2.7.0.

Three surfaces, three jobs:
- **Primer** (`Primer.md`, new). The forward handoff. Most Alive Next Move, In Execution, Active Commitments, Parked, Session Opener. Read first, every session.
- **Sovereign Command.** The minimal live-signal glance. Stays short. Gets only a light touch at close.
- **Git commit body.** The backward record of what each session did. Git is the log.

## What It Adds / Changes

**New: the Primer (`Primer.md` at repo root).**
- Pre-loaded with onboarding orientation. A fresh download opens to a Primer that points the Sovereign into the Getting Started folder, framed as a flexible path rather than a rigid sequence. As the ecosystem operates, the Closeout reshapes the Primer into the live rolling horizon.
- Sits at the root next to `Sovereign Command.md`. The two session surfaces are siblings: Primer is the fuller forward picture, Sovereign Command is the glance.

**CLAUDE.md wiring.**
- A new Session Start section names the Primer as the first read at every session, ahead of anything else, with Sovereign Command as the live glance and North Star as background. This is what makes the Primer "pre-loaded": the trust anchor points at it, so the orientation surfaces on its own however the Sovereign opens the session.

**Session Closeout SKILL.md rewrite. Three actions, target under 3 minutes:**
- **Breadcrumbs wherever they belong.** Widened from plans-only to any artifact the session directly touched. Second-order ripple-chasing batches to the Autonomous Improvement Session (ships as v2.9.1).
- **Refresh the Primer.** Purge stale Parked items first, rewrite to the rolling horizon, end with a Session Opener line. Then give Sovereign Command its light touch only: drop what resolved, shift the headline if the lead moved.
- **Commit with a readable body.** A 2-3 sentence body (what shipped, key decision, what comes next) is the always-on searchable backward record.

**Retired:**
- The per-session narrative log in `Vault (Archive)/Session Logs/`. No new logs are written. Git is the log.
- The lightweight-versus-full mode binary. The three-worker reconciliation became an escalation tool fired only for a session touching 6 or more plans.
- Any notion of bending Sovereign Command into a session capsule. There is no non-git fallback. The template assumes a git-tracked vault, which is why git is wired into the build. A Sovereign who opts out of git adds their own record surface.

**Frozen:**
- Any existing `Vault (Archive)/Session Logs/Index.md` and its logs become a historical archive. Nothing appends to the index.

**Added:**
- Concurrency-aware staging in the auto-commit step (solo versus concurrent paths) so a sibling session's work never gets swept into the wrong commit.

**Cross-reference cleanup (high-traffic files):**
- AI Interface Activation Protocol: orientation now reads the Primer first, Sovereign Command as the glance, git commit bodies for backward callbacks. The gap-adaptive tier logic and the Continuity Check repointed the same way.
- AI Interface Activation skill: same reordering.
- AI Interface Knowledge Map: Primer added to Core Systems, the session record named as git commit bodies, the Session Logs Index noted as frozen.
- Session Closeout Protocol (doctrine) slimmed to match the skill.

## How to Implement

If you have an existing ecosystem on a prior version:

1. **Add the Primer.** Pull `Primer.md` to your repo root. If your ecosystem is past onboarding, replace the pre-loaded onboarding content with your current rolling horizon (Most Alive, In Execution, Active Commitments, Parked, Session Opener). If you are still onboarding, leave the shipped content and let it guide you.

2. **Wire CLAUDE.md.** Add the Session Start section that names the Primer as the first read at session start. Your AI should open the Primer ahead of anything else.

3. **Replace the Session Closeout skill and its protocol.** Pull the new `Council Chamber/Skills/Session Closeout/SKILL.md` and `Council Chamber/Protocols/Session/Session Closeout Protocol.md`. Run the three-action close from here forward.

4. **Confirm git is your log.** The commit body is your session record. Stop writing per-session logs. If your vault is not git-tracked, either start (recommended, it is why git is in the build) or add your own record surface. Do not use Sovereign Command for it.

5. **Freeze your Session Logs.** Leave any existing `Vault (Archive)/Session Logs/` and its `Index.md` in place as a historical archive. Do not append again.

6. **Repoint activation reads.** Anything that reads the Session Logs Index for callbacks repoints to the Primer plus git commit bodies. This update fixes the high-traffic files in the template. Grep your ecosystem for `Session Logs/Index` and repoint the rest in one pass. Likely carriers:
   - `Council Chamber/AI Interface/AI Interface Knowledge Map.md`
   - `Council Chamber/Protocols/AI Interface/AI Interface Activation Protocol.md`
   - `Council Chamber/Skills/AI Interface Activation/SKILL.md`
   - Any weekly review or weekly story skill that reads the log index. Repoint to `git log`.

## Prerequisites

Foundation build complete. A git-tracked vault, since git is the session record. Sovereign Command in use as the live glance (ships from early versions).

## Optional?

No. The Primer and the Session Closeout are foundational. The Primer is what keeps the close fast and Sovereign Command minimal.
